tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain executions, agent runs, prompt versions, and dataset evaluations within LangChain and LangGraph ecosystems
features: End-to-end trace visualization for LangChain apps
Token usage and latency tracking per run
tools.pricing: Free tier: 5,000 traces/month. Developer: $39/month for 50,000 traces. Plus: $99/month for 200,000 traces. Enterprise: custom pricing. Additional traces billed per usage.
tools.best_for: Teams building production apps with LangChain or LangGraph who need deep tracing, prompt management, and evaluation workflows in a tightly integrated environment

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests and responses, token consumption, costs, latency, error rates, and user-level usage across multiple providers
features: One-line integration via proxy or async logging
Request caching to reduce redundant API calls
Rate limiting and spend controls per user or session
Multi-provider support including OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, and Gemini
tools.pricing: Free tier: 100,000 requests/month. Pro: $20/month for 1,000,000 requests. Team: $200/month with advanced features. Enterprise: custom pricing. Usage-based overages apply.
tools.best_for: Startups and indie developers who need quick LLM cost visibility and caching with minimal setup, especially when working across multiple providers

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: ML and LLM experiments, model training runs, prompt evaluations, traces, dataset versions, and model performance metrics at scale
features: Experiment tracking and comparison across runs
Integration with major ML frameworks and LLM providers
tools.pricing: Free tier: unlimited personal projects with limited team features. Teams: $50/user/month. Enterprise: custom pricing. Storage and compute costs may apply separately.
tools.best_for: ML engineering teams that need both traditional model training observability and LLM monitoring in a unified platform with strong experiment tracking heritage

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: LLM performance, hallucination rates, retrieval quality, embedding drift, prompt and response analysis, and production model health for both LLM and traditional ML
features: RAG pipeline evaluation including retrieval relevance and faithfulness
A/B testing for prompts and models
tools.pricing: Free tier available with limited data retention. Growth plans start around $50/month. Enterprise pricing is custom based on data volume and features. Phoenix (open-source version) is free to self-host.
tools.best_for: Enterprise ML and AI teams that need rigorous production monitoring, RAG quality evaluation, and compliance-ready observability across both LLM and classical ML systems

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, token costs, user sessions, evaluation scores, and feedback signals for any LLM application regardless of framework
features: Framework-agnostic tracing via SDK or API
Prompt management with versioning and rollback
Cost and token tracking per trace and session
Dataset management for testing and fine-tuning
Integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and OpenAI SDK
tools.pricing: Open-source self-hosted version is free. Cloud Hobby: free with limited retention. Pro: $59/month for increased limits. Team: $199/month. Enterprise: custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Developers and teams who want open-source flexibility with the option to self-host for data privacy, while still getting full-featured tracing and prompt management

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token usage, latency, and request metadata using OpenTelemetry standards, compatible with any observability backend that supports OTLP
features: Auto-instrumentation for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, LangChain, and more
Vendor-agnostic: exports to Datadog, Grafana, Jaeger, and other OTLP backends
tools.pricing: Completely free and open-source. Costs depend only on the observability backend you choose to export data to (e.g., Datadog, Grafana Cloud).
tools.best_for: Engineering teams already invested in OpenTelemetry infrastructure who want to add LLM observability without adopting a new vendor, using their existing monitoring stack

cost_tips: Implement semantic caching to store and reuse responses for similar or identical prompts, reducing redundant API calls by up to 40-60% in applications with repetitive query patterns

Choose the smallest model capable of handling your task by benchmarking GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku, or Gemini Flash against larger models for your specific use case, as smaller models can cost 10-20x less per token with comparable quality on focused tasks

Optimize prompt engineering by removing redundant instructions, using concise system prompts, and setting appropriate max_tokens limits to cap response length, since every token in both input and output contributes directly to your bill

Implement request batching and asynchronous processing where real-time responses are not required, and use streaming responses combined with early stopping logic to terminate generation as soon as the needed content is received
